Check with `python T18_scratch/t18_calib_item3.py` or directly: sum `matched` from defake_gate.data_section_digests against build/GUNE5D/report.json's units[].measures.matched_data for the same unit.
subject: tool:defake-gate
value:
THE PROJECT'S DATA MEASURE IS ALL-OR-NOTHING PER SECTION, SO ANY GATE THAT NETS MATCHED DATA PER BYTE IS AN UPPER BOUND THAT READS +0 ON A WHOLE-SECTION LOSS. The PROGRESS `Data:` line comes from build/GUNE5D/report.json, and objdiff counts a data section as matched only when it matches ENTIRELY: one wrong byte contributes the section's FULL size to a per-byte accounting and ZERO to the image's.

MEASURED, on game/ui/btext, whose extabindex is one byte off:
  defake_gate per-section byte accounting  extab 248/248, extabindex 371/372, TOTAL 619/620
  report.json main/game/ui/btext           matched_data=248  total_data=620
  all-or-nothing recomputation             248/620   (agrees with report.json)
The gate's own baseline printout therefore overstated matched Data by 371 of 620 bytes on ONE TU, and a keep that destroyed the 248-byte extab match while repairing a single byte of extabindex would have netted +1 against the image's -248.

THE SCALE, over all 168 unit pairs the gate can price: 91 units and 134 sections DISAGREE between the two accountings, for 30,920 bytes of matched Data overstated in total -- game/sound/sounds_evt 2,173 -> 0, game/anim/action 2,340 -> 220, game/game/player 1,386 -> 0, game/enemy/critter 1,369 -> 0. 77 units and 326 sections are identical either way.

THE ALL-OR-NOTHING RULE IS A LOWER BOUND, NOT A REPRODUCTION, AND THAT IS THE SAFE DIRECTION. Validated against report.json's `matched_data` over the 129 units whose section set objdump -s covers (a bss-family section carries no contents and `.init` is not counted as data): 110 reproduce it EXACTLY, 18 UNDER-count it because objdiff credits data at SYMBOL granularity and RESOLVES RELOCATIONS -- a section holding a pointer table is credited there while its raw bytes differ here -- and 1 over-counts by 16 bytes (Runtime.PPCEABI.H/NMWException). A gate must under-credit rather than manufacture a pass; the per-byte form did exactly the opposite.

A symbol-level rule was measured and is WORSE (105 of 129 exact), because dtk's target symbol names (lbl_/jumptable_) do not correspond to our `@N` pool entries and relocation-filled tables read as zeros in our object.

THE GENERAL FORM: when a gate prices a change against a project-level measure, it must price it in THAT MEASURE'S UNITS. A finer accounting is not a conservative approximation of a coarser one -- here it is strictly more optimistic, and the direction of the error is what decides whether a gate can pass a loss.
